geometry.title: Raw Data vs Closures Computed
geometry.description: Raw Data View shows the raw survey and stays editable. Closures Computed View shows the least-squares solve across loop closures and is read-only. Plan and Export force it. Available only when the project has eligible closures.

tools.title: Tool Palette
tools.description: Your editing tools. The move tools drag geometry and connected shots follow.

displayOptions.title: Display Options
displayOptions.description: Every layer toggle lives here: satellite imagery, grid, labels, color overlays, and the geometry switch above.

docks.title: The Three Docks
docks.description: The map is the same map in every mode. What surrounds it changes with the mode.
descriptionItems: Left: sections. Double-click one to frame it.
Right: detail for the selection, or the gas plan in Plan mode.
Bottom: the shot table. Double-click a row to frame it.

done.title: That is the tour
done.description: This tour runs once. The guides for DMP import and station placement still appear the first time you reach those workflows. Settings > General > Restart onboarding replays all of them.

selection.title: Choose Sections
selection.description: Pick which DMP sections to import. Single-shot sections are deselected by default. Surveyor and date defaults above apply to everything you select.

zeroDatumSelection.title: Pick the Anchor Section
zeroDatumSelection.description: A zero datum ties one station to a real-world GPS position, so every other section can be placed relative to it. Pick the section that should carry it, or skip to position everything manually and set it later.

zeroDatum.title: GPS Anchor
zeroDatum.description: Anchor one station to real-world coordinates. Optional - you can skip it and set it later. Accepted formats:
descriptionItems: DD, DMS, DDM, UTM, MGRS, Plus Codes
Pasted Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, or Bing links

suggestedConnection.title: Suggested Connections
suggestedConnection.description: Stalagmight scores likely overlaps from reference shots and geometry, then proposes a station-to-station merge. Check the confidence, then confirm or skip to place manually.
descriptionItems: Overlap handling: Interpolate, Keep Original, Keep Connected, or Keep Both.

segmentPlacement.title: Placing What Did Not Connect
segmentPlacement.description: Segments with no confident match land here. Choose per segment:
descriptionItems: From existing station: anchor to a station you pick.
Place on map: position it by hand.
Do not place: skip this segment entirely.

placeOnMap.title: Click to Place, Hover to Snap
placeOnMap.description: Click the map to drop the section; position can be refined later. Hovering near an existing station snaps and merges the two at placement time.
descriptionItems: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.
Once this guide closes, Esc reopens the placement options and metadata.

items.pan: Move the map view without editing data.
items.zoom: Box-zoom to focus on an area. Left/right click zooms in/out.
items.moveStation: Reposition a station; connected shots follow.
items.moveSegment: Move a group of connected sections.

adopt.confirmBody: "{{name}}" is an Ariane (.tml) project. Adopting it imports its survey into a new Stalagmight file, uploads that file to SpeleoDB, and links it to this project. Adopting takes the write lock for as long as it runs, and hands it back when the upload is done.
adopt.confirmConsequence: The project type on SpeleoDB is changed to "Stalagmight", and from now on only Stalagmight edits are recognized - later Ariane (.tml) edits are disregarded. To undo this, you will have to manually roll back to the Ariane-only version and change the project type in the SpeleoDB interface.
adopt.doneToast: Project adopted and uploaded to SpeleoDB.
adopt.doneToastNoTypeFlip: Project adopted and uploaded, but its SpeleoDB type could not be changed to "Stalagmight" (you may not have write access).
adopt.doneToastLocalOnly: Project adopted on this machine only - it could not be uploaded. Use Start editing, then Done, to push it to SpeleoDB.
adopt.doneToastLockHeld: Project adopted and uploaded to SpeleoDB, but handing the write lock back could not be confirmed. Your survey is safe on the server; check the SpeleoDB menu and release the lock if you still hold it, so others can edit.
adopt.doneToastLockHeldNoTypeFlip: Project adopted and uploaded to SpeleoDB, but two things are unfinished: handing the write lock back could not be confirmed, and its SpeleoDB type could not be changed to "Stalagmight". Your survey is safe on the server; check the SpeleoDB menu and release the lock if you still hold it, and change the type in SpeleoDB so the project stops offering to be adopted.

dumpPicker.body: This SpeleoDB project holds more than one openable file, so Stalagmight cannot tell which one is the survey. Pick the one you want.
dumpPicker.consequence: The file you choose becomes the project. The next time you push, it replaces the project file on SpeleoDB - so if you are not sure which one is current, check the sizes and dates below, or ask whoever uploaded them. To stop being asked, remove the extra file(s) on SpeleoDB, leaving a single one.

restore.consequence: The restore is kept as unsaved edits on top of the current version; push to make it the project's latest. Your project history is not rewritten.

restore.discardWarning: The working copy has changes that are not on SpeleoDB - including any earlier restore you have not pushed. Restoring this revision replaces them, and they are not on the server, so this cannot be undone.

unwind.title: Unwind to previous SpeleoDB version
unwind.bodyCurrent: Load the edit history stored with revision {{sha}}. Your survey does not change - the operations that produced it come back, so you can keep undoing them one at a time.
unwind.bodyAncestor: Check the survey out to revision {{sha}} and load the edit history stored with it, so you can keep undoing from there.
unwind.consequenceCurrent: The history is downloaded from SpeleoDB. Anything you have not pushed is replaced by that revision.
unwind.consequenceAncestor: This moves the survey back. SpeleoDB has no revert, so pushing afterwards records the older survey as a new revision rather than removing the newer ones.
unwind.failed: Could not load the earlier history.
unwind.discardWarning: This copy holds changes you have not pushed. Unwinding replaces it with revision {{sha}}, so those changes and the current edit history are discarded - including any steps you have undone but not yet redone.

rewind.title: Redo into next SpeleoDB version
rewind.bodyNext: Load the edit history stored with revision {{sha}}, the next version forward, so you can keep redoing from there.
rewind.bodyLatest: Step forward to the latest version and load the edit history stored with it, returning this copy to where the walk started.
rewind.consequence: The history is downloaded from SpeleoDB, replacing the version currently loaded. Nothing is lost: every step came from a revision the server still holds, so you can walk back again.

unreadable.title: The copy on this computer could not be read
unreadable.message: "{{name}}" has already been opened on this computer, but that local copy could not be read, so we cannot tell whether it has changes SpeleoDB has never seen. A save may have been interrupted, or another program may be using it. The file may also be damaged. Nothing has been downloaded yet.
unreadable.keepHint: Keeping the local copy downloads nothing and overwrites nothing. Opening it lets an interrupted save roll back to the last one that finished; if another program is using the file, close it first.
unreadable.discardWarning: Taking the server copy permanently replaces the copy of "{{name}}" on this computer. It could not be read, so any changes in it that are not on SpeleoDB would be lost, and this cannot be undone.
